sentences.text: Noripterus is a genus of dsungaripterid pterodactyloid pterosaur whose name means "lake wing".
This animal possessed long, narrow neck vertebrae, a crest, and a toothless front lower jaw.
The teeth present in Noripterus were well-developed and spaced far apart.
It had a straight, sharp snout that did not point upwards like that of Dsungaripterus.
Noripterus was estimated to be one-third shorter than the contemporaneous Dsungaripterus.
Noripterus was first named by Yang Zhongjian in 1973.
The type species, Noripterus complicidens, was found in the Lianmuqin and Shengjinkou Formations of the Junggar Basin in Xinjiang, China.
The species Noripterus parvus was recovered from the Tsagaantsav Formation of Mongolia.
Researchers suggest Dsungaripterus hunted in shallow lakes eating hard-shelled animals, while Noripterus fed on fish in deeper lake regions.
Noripterus is assigned to the family Dsungaripteridae due to its similarity to Dsungaripterus.
A 2019 study by Kellner and colleagues recovered Noripterus outside Azhdarchoidea within Tapejaroidea as a sister taxon to Dsungaripterus.

The genus Phobetor was originally described by Natasha Bakhurina in 1982 based on a single leg bone, but the name was unavailable because it was previously used as a synonym for the fish Gymnocanthus tricuspis. In 2009, Lü and colleagues found Phobetor indistinguishable from Noripterus and referred it as a junior synonym.
Noripterus lived from the Valanginian to the Barremian, between 137.05 and 121.4 million years ago.
Noripterus lived alongside the larger Dsungaripterus in environments with extensive inland lake systems.
Data suggests at least some deposits containing Noripterus date to the middle Valanginian, though the exact age bounds remain unclear.
It is likely that Noripterus and Dsungaripterus occupied separate ecological niches due to differences in skull robustness and tooth strength.
